160	# AppImageLauncher — desktop integration for AppImages
161	#
162	# Strategy (in order):
163	#   1. PPA `ppa:appimagelauncher-team/stable` — preferred on 20.04/22.04.
164	#   2. GitHub `.deb` fallback — PPA is known-broken on Ubuntu 24.04 "noble"

166	#      GitHub `.deb` still installs cleanly.
167	#   3. AppImageLauncher **Lite** — a user-level AppImage that integrates

169	#
170	# Docs: see docs/tools/appimage.md for install paths, ail-cli usage, and
171	# the libfuse2 / AppArmor gotchas on recent Ubuntu.
172	# =============================================================================
173	
174	- name: Check if AppImageLauncher is installed (system-wide)
175	  when:
176	    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
177	    - target_architecture != 'armv7l'
178	  ansible.builtin.command: dpkg -s appimagelauncher

180	  changed_when: false

182	
183	- name: Install AppImageLauncher via PPA
184	  when:

188	    - ail_check.rc != 0

190	  tags: [sudo]
191	  block:
192	    - name: Add AppImageLauncher PPA
193	      ansible.builtin.apt_repository:
194	        repo: ppa:appimagelauncher-team/stable
195	        state: present
196	        update_cache: true
197	        filename: appimagelauncher-team-stable
198	      ignore_errors: true
199	      register: ail_ppa
200	
201	    - name: Install appimagelauncher from PPA
202	      ansible.builtin.apt:
203	        name: appimagelauncher
204	        state: present
205	      when: ail_ppa is succeeded
206	      register: ail_apt_install
207	      ignore_errors: true
208	  rescue:
209	    - name: Warn AppImageLauncher PPA install failed
210	      ansible.builtin.debug:

212

214	  when:
215	    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
216	    - target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'aarch64']
217	    - not (gui_apps_linux_no_root | bool)
218	    - ail_check.rc != 0
219	    - (ail_apt_install is not defined) or (ail_apt_install is not succeeded)
220	  become: true

222	  block:
223	    - name: Get latest AppImageLauncher release metadata

# https://www.chezmoi.io/reference/special-files/chezmoi-format-tmpl/

# Implied parent dirs of managed files / externals (e.g. ~/.local when only
# ~/.local/share/toolkami/toolkami.rb is managed) inherit mode from
# `0o777 & ~umask`. Default umask is the user's login umask, which on macOS
# (002 → 0775) and various Linux distros (022 → 0755 / 0700 for ~) differs,
# producing recurring "mode-only diff" noise on .local and friends across
# the fleet. Pin umask to 022 so implied dirs are always 0755 regardless of
# host login umask. Files that need stricter modes use the `private_` prefix
# explicitly.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-04-23 14:48:52Z)**_

Yes confirmed — that's not a dotfiles issue. The lock holder is Ubuntu's `unattended-upgrades` background service (PID 2154 still running `unattended-upgrade-shutdown --wait-for-signal`; the 273802 was probably its sibling that grabbed the lock first). It runs automatically after boot and login on a fresh Ubuntu and routinely blocks the first `chezmoi apply`.

But it **does** explain your other questions: ansible aborted on the `base` role before ever reaching `gui_apps_linux`, so Alacritty + AppImageLauncher were never even attempted.

Here's how each piece lines up:

**1. Apt lock (blocker for everything else)**
Two options. Quick: wait for `unattended-upgrades` to finish (`sudo systemctl status unattended-upgrades; pgrep -af unattended-upgrade`) and re-run `chezmoi update --init`. Durable: add `lock_timeout: 600` to the `ansible.builtin.apt:` calls in `base`, `gui_apps_linux`, `devtools`, etc. — apt then *waits* up to 10 min for the lock instead of failing at 60s. Worth doing; this will recur on every fresh-machine bootstrap.

**2. Alacritty + AppImageLauncher**
Already in `gui_apps_linux` role (alacritty via cargo, AppImageLauncher via PPA → .deb fallback, libfuse2 for AppImage runtime). Should appear automatically on the next successful run. Cargo build of alacritty takes ~5–10 min — expected.

**3. Shift+Enter for newline**
`dot_config/alacritty/alacritty.toml:8-11` already maps it to `\u001b[13;2u` (CSI-u). **gnome-terminal cannot do this** — it has no remap mechanism, this is a long-standing upstream limitation. So the fix is "install Alacritty (or Ghostty/Kitty/WezTerm) and stop using gnome-terminal for coding agents." Once gui_apps_linux runs, you'll have Alacritty.

**4. Hack font in gnome-terminal**
Doable via `gsettings set org.gnome.Terminal.Legacy.Profile:/org/gnome/terminal/legacy/profiles:/:<UUID>/ font 'Hack Nerd Font Mono 12'` + `use-system-font false`, wrappable as an ansible task in `gui_apps_linux`. But given (3), if you're going to switch to Alacritty anyway, gnome-terminal styling is wasted effort.

**Recommended order**: (a) wait/kill unattended-upgrades and re-run so gui_apps lands; (b) add `lock_timeout: 600` to apt tasks so this doesn't bite the next fresh machine; (c) skip gnome-terminal font work, use Alacritty. Want me to do (b)? And do you want a pitfall entry under `pitfalls/` for the apt-lock symptom?

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-04-23 14:53:11Z)**_

**(a) Don't kill — the lock is already free.** The error showed PID 273802 holding it, but that process has since exited. The remaining `unattended-upgrade-shutdown --wait-for-signal` (PID 2154) is just a shutdown coordinator and doesn't hold any apt lock; `unattended-upgrades.service` is `active` only in the systemd-tracked sense (it's a long-lived helper). Just re-run `chezmoi update --init` now and it should pass `base`.

For future occurrences, the safe pattern is `sudo systemctl stop unattended-upgrades apt-daily apt-daily-upgrade` (graceful, dpkg-clean) **never** `kill -9` — interrupting a mid-transaction `dpkg`/`apt-get` leaves the package DB half-configured and you have to `sudo dpkg --configure -a` to recover. The `--wait-for-signal` helper is harmless and can be left alone.

**(c) gnome-terminal: font yes, keymap no.**

- **Font**: doable via `gsettings` against the default profile UUID (`dconf read /org/gnome/terminal/legacy/profiles:/default` → set `use-system-font false` + `font 'Hack Nerd Font Mono 12'`). Easy to wrap as a non-sudo ansible task in `gui_apps_linux`.
- **Keymap**: **not possible.** VTE (the widget gnome-terminal builds on) has no API to map a key to a custom escape sequence. The only "shortcuts" gnome-terminal exposes are hardcoded actions (copy/paste/new-tab/zoom). You cannot make Shift+Enter send `\u001b[13;2u` from inside gnome-terminal. People sometimes hack it at the X11/keyd layer, but those are system-wide, fragile, and Wayland-broken — the right fix is to use a terminal that supports remapping (Alacritty/Ghostty/Kitty/WezTerm), which we already configure.

So: gnome-terminal is fine as a *fallback* console (we can give it the right font), but for actual coding-agent / tmux work you want Alacritty. Want me to add the gsettings font task + the `lock_timeout: 600` apt fix in one pass?
